newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tourism earns Tanzania $322 million in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Tourism earns Tanzania $322 million in 1996.

text.p: Tourism, Tanzania's biggest hard currency earner, raised $322 million in 1996 up from $258 million the year before, a government official said on Thursday.

Johnson Manase, senior information officer for the Tanzania Tourist Board, told Reuters that some 326,000 tourists visited Tanzania in 1996 accounting for about five percent of gross national product.
The government of the cash-strapped east African nation has ambitious plans for the sector and hopes to attract up to 500,000 tourists in the year 2000 with projected income of up to $500 million.

"We are on target. Even the World Tourism Organisation (WTO) in Madrid acknowledges growth in tourism for Tanzania last year (1996) was 10.5 percent compared to a world average of 4.5 percent," said Manase.
He attributed the increase in tourist arrivals to an aggressive overseas marketing and promotion campaign launched last year by the government to put Tanzania on the world tourism map.
Manase said the government had boosted security in Tanzania's northern tourist circuit following an attack by bandits earlier this year on a tour party in the Serengeti park.
Police now operate mobile patrols equipped with two-way radios and a special surveillance helicopter was based in the park area, he said.
"The situation is now very safe for tourists -- there's no problems. Security is a priority for visitors," Manase said.

He admitted that roads and infrastructure in Tanzania's main tourism regions were inadequate and said some funds from the 1997/98 budget were earmarked for road improvements in the Serengeti and Ngorongoro area.
